# Retrospective: PR 12797

## What worked
Fresh native sessions and equivalent neutral assignments yielded two genuinely independent wrapper-level investigations. Testing one layer below the added stub exposed a harmless numeric-status mismatch while confirming the actual production path. Baseline negative controls established the new test's relevance. A small comparison replaces dense retry narration in the delivered comment.

## Friction and improvements
Fable's original scenario delimiter collided with its mode syntax, producing exit-127 setup failures. These were explicitly excluded and corrected in a separate plan. Prefer structured case inputs and preflight a recovery case before long scenario batches. This was a fixture bug, not an Omarchy bug.

Repeated full source/Node snapshots made Fable's preserved evidence roughly 4GB. Future assignments can use explicit minimal source scopes and group cases in one sealed execution, while preserving standalone Node identity and all raw outputs. Do not retroactively prune these sealed bundles.

## Editorial judgment
The observed default retry delay is useful context, but no evidence establishes that an arbitrary tighter cap is better. Preserve the 105-second synthetic-stall condition as a limitation without turning it into an invented production defect or filler suggestion. Preserve disagreement about presentation in the local report.

## Tool issues and resources
No confirmed Omadev or review.py bug. No desktop slots requested, no browser/page opening, no network fixture traffic, and no host mutations. Sandboxes exited and private runtimes were removed. Preserve source worktrees, historical sessions, corrected and failed evidence, and reviewer panes. Final editorial check uses a new Astra Medium native session and exact draft/requirements hashes.

## Carry forward
Keep checking actual wrapper exit behavior, postconditions/call arguments, idempotent retry assumptions, and negative controls. Reviewers own isolated tests and cleanup; outer assistant owns publication and next-session assignment.
comment:
**Verified:** No actionable issue found in the tested scope at `0f0a65b178f0d48dd1a6f9b3321f7458831c3c22`. `omarchy-bar put` now recovers when a timed-out IPC call is followed by a ready shell.

Production `omarchy-bar` and `omarchy-shell`, with synthetic `qs` responses and real timeouts:

| Response sequence | Baseline | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Timeout, then ready | Fails on first call | Retries successfully |
| Persistent timeout | Fails immediately | Fails after retry budget |
| Timeout, then shell absent | Fails | Still fails, not silently skipped |
| Unsupported method | Fails | Still fails |

The added regression test passes on head and fails against baseline production code. An isolated run of the Elsewhen migration with package installation mocked likewise changes from failing on the first timed-out placement to completing on retry.

**Retry limit:** With a continuously unresponsive synthetic `qs` and default settings, failure took about 105 seconds (50 attempts), versus 2 seconds on baseline. Recovery is bounded, but a persistently hung shell now delays the error.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection, baseline/head command tests, and regression-test negative controls. No live desktop, actual plugin-rebuild load, or complete system update was exercised; successful IPC replies do not establish rendered widget placement.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Initial Astra inspection, independent Fable 5.1 and separate Astra reviews, followed by verification of claims against targeted evidence.
